Behind the Scenes: A Private Studio Visit with Artist Melissa Joseph & Curator Sadaf Padder

An intimate studio visit with artist Melissa Joseph, led by independent curator and art advisor Sadaf Padder, at the Elizabeth Foundation for the Arts in Manhattan.

The experience

Join independent curator and art advisor Sadaf Padder for an intimate, behind-the-scenes visit with acclaimed contemporary artist Melissa Joseph at her studio at the Elizabeth Foundation for the Arts in Manhattan.

Guests will gain insight into Joseph’s artistic practice, exploring the history of felting and its relationship to broader ecologies. The visit offers an opportunity to engage directly with the artist about her creative process and learn about studio visit etiquette in a welcoming, conversational setting.

Your hosts

The artist & the curator.

The Artist

Melissa Joseph

Melissa Joseph is a New York-based artist of Indian and Irish descent whose work explores family histories, memory and the cultural experiences of diasporic life. Known for her distinctive use of needle-felted wool and found objects, Joseph draws on personal narratives and craft traditions.

Her work has been shown at the Brooklyn Museum, ICA San Francisco, the Utah Museum of Contemporary Art and at Rockefeller Center, presented by Art Production Fund. She is the recipient of the Brooklyn Museum’s 2025 UOVO Prize and a 2026 NYFA/NYSCA Fellowship, and a regular contributor to BOMB Magazine. Her recent solo exhibitions include Tender at the Brooklyn Museum (2025) and Casserole Culture at Charles Moffett Gallery (2026).

Permanent collections include

Brooklyn MuseumRISD MuseumICA MiamiRuby CityAkron Art MuseumFlint Institute of Arts

The Curator

Sadaf Padder

Sadaf Padder is a Brooklyn-based curator, writer, educator and art advisor whose work examines how artistic ideas travel across cultures, histories and geographies. Through exhibitions, research and writing, she explores cultural memory, Islamic visual cultures and the ways contemporary artists revisit historical traditions to envision alternative futures.

“Belonging is something assembled through stories, objects, and memory rather than a fixed place.”

Her recent curatorial projects include Bounty at Sargent’s Daughters and Mad Heart, Be Brave at Fridman Gallery. Her writing has appeared in Artsy, Hyperallergic, ARTnews and Cultured, and she was a 2022–23 Hyperallergic Arts Writing Fellow. As an advisor, she has facilitated acquisitions for institutions including the RISD Museum and the Baltimore Museum of Art. She is the founder of Alpha Arts Alliance and serves on the boards of the Vera List Center for Art and Politics, Twelve Gates Arts and Grown in Haiti.
